source.title: Discrete vs. Continuous: A Comprehensive Study of Unified Audio Understanding in LALMs
source.authors: Jing Peng; Zi-Chao Nie; Zhi-Sheng Zhang; Jing-Ran Xie; Zhi-Yong Wu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present, but some figure and table content is garbled or flattened in the text extraction. Table 3’s ASR values and headings are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream-task performance across model scales and reports both an ASR setting where scaling laws hold and regressions in many other configurations, qualifying the claim that downstream performance improves predictably with scale.
record.gate_note: The study tests backbone scaling on audio downstream tasks, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy or compute-optimal allocations. Table 3 reports further task scores, but only the ASR columns are used here because the remaining extracted values do not align reliably with the table headings. Values used to select encoder settings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study compares downstream audio-task scores across LLM backbone sizes (SmolLM2 135M/360M with LoRA; Llama-3 1B/8B frozen with a trained projector). That bears on V6 in a new setting: audio understanding through a text-pretrained backbone. It is a weak test. There are only two sizes per family, no fitted curve, no link to pretraining loss, and the 1B and 8B Llama models differ in training recipe, not just size. T3 fits better than T5: the inverse-scaling result is a finding in a new setting, not an argument against the version as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely correct. The authors' main emphasis is that encoder semantic quality sets a performance ceiling: backbone scaling fails to compensate for low semantic density and often regresses in data-limited tasks. Scaling laws hold only for data-abundant LS-960 ASR. The MLP projector is flagged as a possible bottleneck.
record.recipe_differences: This is an audio-understanding benchmark comparing task performance across a small number of backbone sizes, not a held-out text-pretraining cross-entropy sweep with power-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling outcome varies with task/data availability; the paper distinguishes data-abundant LS-960 ASR from many data-limited scenarios.
record.problems: The study measures downstream audio-task scores rather than held-out language-model pretraining loss. It compares only two backbone sizes within each model family and does not fit scaling exponents or predictive curves. The authors note that the simple MLP projector may bottleneck scaling gains. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported scaling comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table 3 downstream-task values are omitted because the extracted table content does not align reliably with its headings; only the ASR columns can be assigned confidently. No result files or other scaling measurements are reported outside Tables 2–3 and §4.2.

untested.parts: Predictability: no curve is fitted and only two sizes are used per family. No relation to pretraining loss is tested. No text-only downstream tasks are tested. Scale is confounded with differing training recipes between Llama-3 1B and 8B.

missing.what: Non-ASR columns for Llama-3 1B vs 8B. The readable values suggest IEMOCAP ER fell for all four encoders (e.g., WavLM 64.06 to 62.29). CREMA-D rose for three encoders but fell for DAC (36.24 to 29.85). A column that appears to be SLURP IC fell for all four (e.g., 71.23 to 70.13). Clotho FENSE fell for three of four. UrbanSound8K, GTZAN and SDD are mixed. Column alignment is uncertain because of flattening, but the values are largely readable.
SmolLM2-135M vs 360M domain-average scores (Speech/Sound/Music/Overall) per encoder. Only part of the 360M block is extracted, but some comparisons are readable (e.g., Whisper speech 0.858 vs 0.807).

record.verdict_notes: V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. This is not one of the original sources. The evidence is two-point comparisons within two model families, so it shows only the direction of change with scale, not whether the improvement is predictable. Several Table 3 values the reader omitted appear readable and mostly point to regression outside ASR. This would strengthen the challenges label if the rows are added.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute; power-law fits and ranges.
Extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its scaling with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests backbone-scale effects on audio downstream tasks, but does not fit predictive curves, relate outcomes to pretraining loss, or test text-only downstream tasks.
No study of fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or dependence on fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Llama-3 frozen-backbone, data-abundant LS-960 ASR (all four encoders), plus LS-100 ASR for HuBERT, WavLM and DAC
relationships.reason: WER is lower at 8B than at 1B (R2, R3, R4, R5, R7, R8, R11). The HuBERT LS-960 gain is small (R1), and the DAC gains occur at WER above 100%.
relationships.display_finding: WER was lower at 8B than 1B, although HuBERT's LS-960 gain was small and DAC gains occurred above 100% WER.

relationships.condition: SmolLM2 135M to 360M with LoRA, across encoders and tasks
relationships.reason: The authors report only marginal gains or fluctuations, which they read as capacity saturation (R9).
relationships.display_finding: Increasing SmolLM2 from 135M to 360M produced only marginal gains or fluctuations across audio encoders and tasks, interpreted as capacity saturation.

relationships.condition: Data-limited tasks under Llama-3 frozen probing, and SpeechTokenizer on LS-100 ASR
relationships.reason: SpeechTokenizer's LS-100 WER rises from 80.82 to 83.40 (R6). Regression occurs in many data-limited scenarios (R12), and about 53% of all configurations regressed (R10). The authors suggest the MLP projector may be a bottleneck.
relationships.display_finding: SpeechTokenizer's LS-100 WER rose from 80.82 to 83.40, and about 53% of all configurations regressed, with an MLP projector bottleneck proposed as an explanation.
